newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel steady to firmer, seeks U.S. direction.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel steady to firmer, seeks U.S. direction.

text.p: NWE cracked fuel oil was steady to a touch firmer on Monday in a market that was waiting for direction from the U.S. following last week's holidays.
Market bulls cited strikes at French oil group Elf which was prompting buying interest, the Portuguese tender and the tight supply situation to support the higher prices.

The bears, not be outdone, said the much vaunted end-user demand had still failed to materialise, that supplies in the Med should be able to meet the EdP tender for up to 75,000 tonnes into January and that Russian straight run material continues to be well offered.

High sulphur cracked barges traded in a range of $122-124 fob ARA with prices slipping a touch towards the end of the day. Dealers said initial enquiries of around 10,000 tonnes did not increase. A cargo was rumoured sold at $123 cif NWE, but several dealers said this price was too much above the market.
Low sulphur cracked cargoes were pegged steady to a touch firmer. A Turkish tender for 25-30k was awarded to a major at an undisclosed level, but a straight run tender was not awarded.
A second half December cargo was offered around $135 fob NWE, a touch above December swap talk of $132.50-$133.50. A French major was looking for a prompt 7,000 tonne cargo.
